extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: Two sets of reliable labels for object recognition experiments: CIFAR-10 with 10 classes and CIFAR-100 with 100 classes, derived from a dataset of millions of tiny colour images.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by searching the web for images of English nouns, followed by a manual filtering process where paid students rejected mislabeled images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were collected from the web using search engines including Google, Flickr, and Altavista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm and using a liberal rejection threshold.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32. Data was preprocessed by multiplying the data matrix by a whitening matrix and deleting the 1000 least significant principal components.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Paid students were given a class and asked to examine images found with that search term and its hyponyms, rejecting images that did not belong to the assigned class based on specific criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors personally verified every label submitted by the labelers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The rough labels provided by the search terms are extremely unreliable due to the nature of online image search technology.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and Testing for object classification experiments.
